top3.headline: Anthropic's Claude Ship reviews, fixes and approves pull requests
top3.whyItMatters: Code approval is now delegable; decide which changes your policy lets an agent sign off.

top3.headline: OpenAI and Cisco open-source Shirudo so agents can shield unpatched systems
top3.whyItMatters: Agents now defend live systems too, buying time between an exploit and a tested patch.

top3.headline: Claude merges connectors and skills into one plugin system
top3.whyItMatters: One plugin format means your company's tools and know-how can be packaged for Claude once.

items.title: GPT-6 Cyber helped validate 948 Linux kernel root bugs in one run
items.takeaway: OpenAI researchers used GPT-6 Cyber to validate the bugs, draft patches for review and work with maintainers upstream.
items.soWhat: Bug discovery now outpaces human patch review; plan for a much larger fix queue.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco release Shirudo, an agent runtime for live defense
items.takeaway: Open-source Linux runtime; agents write dynamic eBPF controls to block exploits while patches are tested.
items.soWhat: Agents can now hold the line on unpatched systems without downtime.

items.title: Claude Code desktop puts files, changes and terminal in tabs
items.takeaway: Redesigned side panel; tabs can move or pop out. Mac first, Windows and Linux coming.
items.soWhat: Agent coding tools are becoming full workspaces, not chat windows.

items.title: a16z tests what makes AI shopping agents choose a product
items.takeaway: Four consumer agents, 1,270 prompts, 11,307 completed runs, with The Prompting Company.
items.soWhat: Specific customer needs can overturn an agent's default pick, so state yours plainly.

items.title: Claude connectors and skills become one plugin system
items.takeaway: Live on Free, Pro, Max and Ultra; Team and Enterprise coming soon. 10,000+ plugins listed.
items.soWhat: Package your tools and know-how once as a plugin, not twice.

items.title: Replit: more agents help, but more compute alone does not
items.takeaway: Replit research on scaling laws for agent swarms; how agents organize matters.
items.soWhat: Design how your agents coordinate before you add more of them.

items.title: Claude Ship reviews, fixes and approves pull requests
items.takeaway: Beta for Team and Enterprise; approvals limited to what team policy allows.
items.soWhat: Write the approval policy now; it defines what the agent may merge.

items.title: Gemini 4 Neon rebuilds Turing's 1936 study in interactive 3D
items.takeaway: Built from archival photos in Antigravity, with a running Universal Turing Machine.
items.soWhat: Models now turn archives into working 3D spaces in one project.

items.title: Claude Platform offers zero data retention with misuse checks
items.takeaway: Public beta for eligible orgs: encrypted Messages API copies go to your own cloud storage.
items.soWhat: You keep the data trail while the vendor keeps none, easing compliance reviews.

voices.quote: The goal is to help you ship code as fast as you can write it.
It lets agents write dynamic eBPF controls to shield systems from exploits, giving defenders more time to test and roll out patches.
Unlike traditional scaling laws, more compute doesn't necessarily translate into better results
Specific customer needs can overturn an agent's default
There’s now one way to connect your tools to Claude, teach it a new skill, or do both.

hotOnX.note: OpenAI's CEO cheering Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, AI's key chip supplier.

hotOnX.text: Introducing Claude Ship (beta): Claude can review your pull requests, work on fixes, and approve the ones your team's policy allows.
hotOnX.note: Letting an agent approve code is a big step in delegation.

hotOnX.text: We’re introducing Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime allowing agents to defend systems without downtime.
hotOnX.note: Agents moving into live security defense, built with Cisco.

hotOnX.text: Connectors and skills come together as plugins. Live on Free, Pro, Max, and Ultra plans.
hotOnX.note: One format for tools and skills simplifies how teams extend Claude.
